_comment: Every place that can show a FrostFile user a scary screen, and the door you knock on.
cadence  per-release = the artifact hash changed, so this must be redone every build.
standing    = a property of the project or domain; done once, carried forward.
vt_engines maps VirusTotal's engine names back to a target so `reputation.py scan`
can say 'Emsisoft flags you -> here is the Emsisoft form'.
public   false = not open to non-customers; recorded so nobody wastes an evening on it.
URLs verified 2026-08-08. Re-verify before a release: vendors retire forms without notice.

targets.name: Dr.Web
targets.turnaround: not published; you get a tracking request ID by email
targets.notes: Best-shaped form in the whole list: explicit 'False positive' category, no login, 100MB limit fits our zip directly, and it emails you a request ID you can chase. Start here.

targets.name: Emsisoft
targets.notes: Dedicated 'False positive — report a wrongly detected file or URL' category. 200MB attachment limit, the most generous found.

targets.name: Webroot (OpenText)
targets.notes: Direct uploader, no login, reason dropdown has 'False Positive detection'. The old standalone vendor-dispute page now redirects to generic support — use this uploader instead. Ticket fallback: https://mysupport.webrootanywhere.com/supportwelcome.aspx

targets.name: Gen Digital whitelist (Norton + Avast + AVG + Avira)
targets.auth: none — free, no Avast subscription needed
targets.notes: DO THIS ONE FIRST. The form states verbatim that files uploaded here are 'valid for all Gen family of consumer brands that include Avast, AVG, Avira and Norton' — four engines cleared by one submission. After approval they issue FTP credentials so future builds are dropped, not re-argued. Excludes cracks/keygens; submit complete files. 60MB web cap, which the FTP route removes.

targets.name: Gen Digital false-positive form (per build, if flagged)
targets.notes: Only needed if a build gets flagged before the whitelist program covers it. Wants the detection name and Alert ID from the user's alert, so ask whoever reported it for a screenshot. Brand-specific front-ends: Norton https://submissions.norton.com/submitsample, AVG https://www.avg.com/en-ww/report-false-positive, Avira https://www.avira.com/en/analysis/submit (or novirus@avira.com).

targets.name: Microsoft Defender
targets.auth: optional, but sign in — you need the ID to chase it
targets.turnaround: medium priority: analyst review within a few days
targets.notes: THE most important AV target — Defender is on by default on every Windows machine, so this is the one that decides whether a family member sees a warning at all. Choose the 'Software developer' radio option, not 'Home customer'. 50MB cap: submit the flagged FrostFile.exe alone, not the onedir zip. Submission details are retained only 30 days.

targets.name: ESET whitelist program (standing)
targets.notes: The cleanest developer arrangement of any vendor. Email whitelist@eset.sk a registration form (company details, product name/description/download URL/platforms) plus technical answers on code signing, packing/obfuscation, and bundled software. They reply with FTP credentials once; thereafter you upload each build to your folder and 'all folders are being scanned regularly'. Answer the packing question honestly — PyInstaller, disclosed, is fine; hiding it is what gets you flagged.

targets.name: ESET false positive (per build, if flagged)
targets.notes: Subject line must clearly say 'False positive'. Zip password-protected with 'infected'. Plain-text email only — no links, images, or signature footer, they get stripped as suspicious. If nothing after 3 days, resend quoting the original subject, date/time and sending address.

targets.name: Kaspersky
targets.notes: Check the file on OpenTIP, then click 'Submit to reanalyze' if you disagree with the verdict. Standing option: the Kaspersky Allowlist Program at kaspersky.com/partners/allowlist-program, though its application mechanics could not be confirmed (the page is client-side rendered) and it wants a company website with a legal address. DEAD URL — do not use whitelisting.kaspersky.com, it now redirects to the homepage.

targets.name: Bitdefender
targets.notes: Use the BUSINESS form — the consumer one sits behind a Cloudflare challenge. Category dropdown has 'False Positive'. 25MB is the tightest cap anywhere, well under our zip, so use the URL field pointing at frostfile.org/download/. The page notes that filling the optional fields shortens the wait, so fill them all.

targets.name: Sophos
targets.auth: guest mode available (Sophos Home logins do NOT work)
targets.turnaround: allow ~15 days, then re-check the verdict yourself
targets.notes: Expect NO ticket, no reply, and no interaction — you submit, wait, and re-query Intelix to see whether the verdict changed. Plan on the download-link route given the size cap. Lab form alternative: support.sophos.com/support/s/filesubmission. is-spam@labs.sophos.com is spam-only, not for file FPs.

targets.name: McAfee (consumer)
targets.notes: You already have an approval here but need to resubmit for the new build. The page serves customers AND software vendors for inclusion in the trusted-clean-file database. Behind an Akamai bot block, so open it in a real browser and confirm the current size cap yourself — a 10MB limit is cited in some sources and would force the URL route. Trellix (enterprise) is now a separate company with its own form.

targets.name: Malwarebytes
targets.notes: Weakest channel of the majors: non-subscribers post publicly in the False Positives forum with the file attached or linked, and staff pick it up. No SLA, no API, no private route. Posting publicly is fine here — the source is public anyway.

targets.name: F-Secure
targets.turnaround: not published; submitted data deleted after 30 days
targets.notes: Explicit 'Harmless file is detected (False Positive)' category. Zip and password-protect with 'infected'. Business route: /en/business/support-and-downloads/submit-a-sample

targets.name: G Data
targets.notes: Covers 'a G DATA product has incorrectly identified a legitimate file as malign'. A 100MB cap appears in third-party sources but is NOT stated on the form itself. URL form: /url?lang=en

targets.name: Trend Micro
targets.notes: Redirects to helpcenter.trendlife.com. Choose 'Something else', pick product, describe the FP. Their site blocks automated fetching, so open it in a real browser. A developer 'detection re-evaluation' page exists at trendmicro.com/en_us/about/legal/detection-reevaluation.html but could not be verified through the WAF — try it manually first.

targets.name: K7
targets.notes: Email is the reliable path here: zip with archive password 'infected' and mail it, or share a Google Drive link — K7's own KB explicitly allows a Drive link, which suits a 75MB zip. The web form's 'False Positive' category is unconfirmed.

targets.name: Fortinet FortiGuard (AV sample)
targets.notes: Email the zip (inner archive password 'infected') to submitvirus@fortinet.com with 'false positive' in the subject. Confirmed from Fortinet's own AVLabs PDF. The web contact form has no file upload.

targets.name: Fortinet classification dispute (software author)
targets.turnaround: automated receipt email; reviewed case by case
targets.notes: The one true 'I am the software author' channel found anywhere. Framed around spyware misclassification but it is the right door for a publisher. Standing, not per-build — it disputes how the PRODUCT is classified.

targets.name: Comodo / Xcitium
targets.notes: The old comodo.com/home/internet-security/submit.php is DEAD (connection refused). Use Xcitium Cloud Verdict, which needs a free registration. A file judged an FP gets added to the Xcitium whitelist.

targets.name: Panda / WatchGuard
targets.notes: WEAKEST channel in the list. The public form is for the IPS engine only (wants a Signature ID, no file upload) and is useless for endpoint AV. Endpoint FPs route through a WatchGuard Cloud customer account. The pandasecurity.com address is community-sourced and UNVERIFIED — try it, expect a bounce, do not spend an evening here.

targets.name: CrowdStrike Falcon
targets.auth: customer tenant account — no public ISV intake exists
targets.notes: MARK AS n/a. There is no vendor-facing 'allowlist my software' intake. Falcon FPs are resolved inside the customer's own console by their admin. If a FrostFile user hits this, the fix is THEIR IT team adding an exclusion — ask them to open the ticket from their tenant. Code signing plus reputation is the only lever we have.

targets.name: SentinelOne
targets.notes: MARK AS n/a. Same as CrowdStrike: support-portal ticket requiring a customer account. report@sentinelone.com is widely cited as the VirusTotal-engine FP contact but is UNVERIFIED against their own docs — cheap to try, do not rely on it.

targets.name: Azure Artifact Signing (was Trusted Signing)
targets.turnaround: individual path: minutes once status flips to Action Required
targets.notes: IN PROGRESS. Renamed from Trusted Signing. The individual path is USA/Canada only and the 3-year entity rule does NOT apply to it — that rule was always organizations-only and no longer appears in the current docs. Watch for status to flip from 'In Progress' to ACTION REQUIRED: that is your cue, and nothing happens until you act. Sign in with the exact email on the request or you get a permissions error. $9.99/mo Basic, billing starts at account creation and is not pro-rated. Check billing account type is 'Individual' with correct legal name BEFORE proceeding — the cert is populated from it, read-only. The verification email link expires in 7 days and cannot be resent.

targets.name: Certum Open Source Code Signing (cloud)
targets.notes: PAYMENT UNCLEAR. Likely cause: there are TWO Open Source SKUs and the €69 card+reader set is currently OUT OF STOCK, which would explain repeated failed checkouts. You want the €49 CLOUD SKU (SimplySign, no hardware). Check shop.certum.eu -> My Account -> My orders; if an order is not listed there, checkout never completed. For duplicate charges email reklamacje@certum.pl (Mon-Fri 08:00-16:00 CET). Note the cryptographic card is non-refundable even on a valid return — another reason to take the cloud SKU. Also needs a utility bill and a public project URL where your name is visibly attached.

targets.name: Microsoft Store (MSIX) — the free, warning-free path
targets.notes: STRONGEST OPTION FOR WINDOWS AND IT IS NOW FREE. Microsoft's own docs: 'The simplest way to avoid SmartScreen warnings is to publish through the Microsoft Store. Store-distributed apps are signed by a Microsoft certificate and are NEVER subject to SmartScreen download warnings.' They re-sign the MSIX, so you never buy or manage a certificate. Registration fees were dropped in 2025-2026 for both account types. MUST start at storedeveloper.microsoft.com — other entry points still show the legacy paid flow. CAVEAT: only works for MSIX; an MSI/EXE installer is NOT re-signed. Individual accounts are framed for distribution 'not in relation to business, trade, or profession', which a free AGPL tool fits.

targets.name: Apple notarization (Developer Program)
targets.notes: $99/yr is the ONLY path to a warning-free Mac download. No open-source waiver exists — the fee waiver explicitly excludes individuals and sole proprietors regardless of licensing. A free Apple ID cannot notarize (it issues only development certs, which notarization rejects). Developer ID Application cert is a PRECONDITION, not an alternative: signed-but-not-notarized shows the SAME scary dialog as unsigned. Sign inside-out (never --deep, deprecated since macOS 13), --options runtime --timestamp, then staple the .app and RE-ZIP with ditto -c -k --keepParent. Shipping the submission zip is the classic mistake: it holds an unstapled app that fails offline.

targets.name: macOS ad-hoc signing (defensive, free)
targets.notes: DO THIS EVEN WITHOUT THE $99. Apple Silicon refuses to execute native arm64 code with no valid signature AT ALL — that is a kernel-level check below Gatekeeper, and 'Open Anyway' cannot rescue it. An ad-hoc signature satisfies it. This buys RUNNABILITY, not a better dialog. PyInstaller's arm64 output is normally ad-hoc signed by the linker already, PROVIDED packaging does not corrupt it — so use 'ditto -c -k --keepParent', never plain zip or Finder Compress, which mangle symlinks and _CodeSignature. A corrupted signature is WORSE than none: it lands in the 'damaged' state where no override appears at all.

targets.name: SmartScreen file reputation (accrues, no door)
targets.turnaround: several weeks and hundreds of clean installs (Microsoft's words)
targets.notes: MARK AS n/a — there is no mechanism to submit for consumer reputation review. Two signals: publisher reputation and file-hash reputation. The reason signing matters is that reputation 'cannot transfer from previous versions unless both were signed using the same publisher identity' — so signing is what makes v1.1 inherit v1.0's standing. Do NOT buy EV: Microsoft removed the EV bypass in 2024 and now states plainly that 'paying a premium for EV solely to avoid SmartScreen warnings is no longer justified'. Note our zip does not shield the exe — Explorer propagates Mark-of-the-Web to extracted files.

targets.name: OpenText Threat Intelligence (BrightCloud)
targets.notes: DO THIS FIRST of all the web targets. Five minutes, no account, fastest published SLA, and BrightCloud is OEM'd into a very large number of third-party firewalls and UTMs — one form reaches many downstream filters. Comments field is capped at 150 characters, so write the justification tight. The old brightcloud.com URL now redirects here.

targets.name: Fortinet FortiGuard web filter
targets.turnaround: not stated on the form (community says ~24h, unconfirmed)
targets.notes: High priority for this audience: FortiGate is the most common firewall in small-to-mid construction firms. No account. Wants the URL, a suggested category from an 80+ dropdown, optional 2MB screenshot, and your name/email/company. Check current rating first at fortiguard.com/webfilter.

targets.name: Symantec / Broadcom WebPulse Site Review
targets.turnaround: no SLA published; Broadcom says it cannot guarantee a rating change
targets.notes: High priority: Symantec/Blue Coat ProxySG is very common at large contractors. No login. Give the suggested category AND a detailed reason the current rating is wrong — the form explicitly asks for justification.

targets.name: Cisco Talos (also covers Umbrella / OpenDNS)
targets.turnaround: no SLA; manually reviewed by an analyst
targets.notes: High leverage — one submission feeds Cisco Umbrella, Secure Web Appliance, and Cisco web reputation. This is ALSO the documented public path for Umbrella/OpenDNS, so there is no separate Umbrella form to file. Suggest up to five categories ordered most-to-least relevant. Separate reputation ticket at /reputation_center/web_reputation. Do NOT use /reputation_center/submit_ticket — it 500s.

targets.name: Trellix / Skyhigh TrustedSource
targets.auth: none for lookup and category suggestion
targets.notes: Since Feb 2024 this and McAfee's sitelookup are SEPARATE databases — you must submit to both to cover enterprise Trellix/Skyhigh gateways and consumer McAfee endpoints. See target mcafee-sitelookup.

targets.name: McAfee SiteLookup (consumer web control)
targets.auth: none for lookup and category suggestion
targets.notes: The consumer half of the Trellix split. Submitting to trustedsource.org does NOT cover this — each site's own banner tells the other vendor's customers to go elsewhere. File both.

targets.name: Microsoft SmartScreen — site reputation
targets.turnaround: not published; you get a confirmation email you can reply to if urgent
targets.notes: The URL above already has frostfile.org base64-encoded into it (verified), so it opens the form ready to go without needing a block page first. Choose 'I am the owner or representative of this website'. Street address and privacy-statement fields are REQUIRED — FrostFile collects nothing, and saying so plainly is a strong answer. One form per URL; duplicates do not expedite. Distinct from the file submission at wdsi/filesubmission.

targets.name: Google Search Console (Safe Browsing review channel)
targets.notes: Verify ownership NOW even though we are clean — this is the appeal channel if Safe Browsing ever flags the site or a hosted binary, and you do not want to be doing DNS verification during an incident. Check current status any time at transparencyreport.google.com/safe-browsing/search. No-account fallback: safebrowsing.google.com/safebrowsing/report_error/

targets.name: Netcraft
targets.notes: Only act if actually flagged — but know that Netcraft is an UPSTREAM FEED. A Netcraft false positive propagates into SmartScreen and Cloudflare, and Netcraft retracting it does NOT clear those downstream. If hit here, clear Netcraft AND separately re-submit to SmartScreen.

targets.name: Barracuda Central
targets.notes: Cheap to file. Website Category Submission section: URL, category dropdown, image captcha. Check current rating at barracudacentral.org/lookups.

targets.name: Palo Alto Networks PAN-DB
targets.auth: try without login; a free account may be required
targets.turnaround: automated crawler may auto-approve immediately; else human review
targets.notes: Search the domain, then click 'Request Change' below the results. Whether the request submits without login is UNCONFIRMED — try unauthenticated first. If their crawler validates your suggestion it is auto-approved, so a clean, obviously-categorizable landing page helps.

targets.name: Zscaler Site Review
targets.notes: File it, but do not count on it: the page is publicly reachable and the docs describe an open flow, yet community posts suggest it is intended for customers routing traffic through Zscaler. Whether a non-customer submission is actioned is UNVERIFIED. Up to three sites and three categories per request.

targets.name: Sophos web categorization
targets.auth: free community account (the support portal needs a paid license)
targets.turnaround: 24-72 hours, most under 24 (stated by Sophos staff)
targets.notes: The support portal URL tab requires a Sophos ID with a valid support license, so as a non-customer post in the Community Chat Discussions forum instead — Sophos staff confirm they respond within 24h on business days and will action the recategorization. Do NOT use sophos.com/reporturl: it redirects then times out.

targets.name: Chrome 'not commonly downloaded' warning
targets.notes: MARK AS n/a AND STOP LOOKING. There is no form, no queue, and no appeal for the uncommon-download warning — it is purely reputation-based. Chrome's developer section routes only to Search Console, which handles affirmative malware flags, not this. Note their 'Unverified' label means the USER has Safe Browsing switched off, which you cannot affect at all. Code signing helps reputation accrue but does NOT clear this on day one. The honest play is download-page copy that warns people it may appear.

targets.name: Forcepoint (formerly Websense)
targets.auth: Forcepoint Customer Hub login — no public path
targets.notes: MARK AS n/a. Customer-only. Every guide pointing at csi.forcepoint.com or csi.websense.com is stale — those hostnames are NXDOMAIN and no longer resolve. If a firm reports a Forcepoint block, ask THEM to submit it from inside their support account; it takes them two minutes.

targets.name: DMARC reporting (Cloudflare DMARC Management)
targets.notes: FIX NEEDED: _dmarc.frostfile.org currently reads 'v=DMARC1; p=none; rua=mailto:updates@frostfile.org' — aggregate reports are being dumped as gzipped XML into the same mailbox that IS the subscriber list. Cloudflare DMARC Management is free on all plans, needs only that the zone use Cloudflare DNS (it does), and renders the XML as readable analytics.

targets.name: DMARC policy: none -> quarantine -> reject
targets.notes: SPF and DKIM are already correct (spf.privateemail.com; DKIM selector 'privateemail'), so the runway is short. Sit at p=none 4-6 weeks reading reports, then quarantine, then reject with sp=reject. Worth doing: frostfile.org is exactly the domain a 'download this update' phish would spoof, aimed at non-technical users.

targets.name: Google Postmaster Tools
targets.notes: Set it up once and then forget it. Google suppresses data below a privacy threshold, so at a few hundred recipients a few times a year the dashboards will be empty essentially always. Do not troubleshoot the blank charts — it is working as designed.

targets.name: Pre-send deliverability check
targets.notes: Before each release email: send the REAL draft to the mail-tester address (3 free tests/24h, aim for 10/10), then to a personal Gmail and check More > Show original for three PASSes with frostfile.org as the domain, then to an Outlook.com and a Yahoo address to see Inbox vs Junk. Those test accounts are the only placement signal available at this volume.
